Charity Governance & Custodianship

About the Charity & Trust

Preserved entirely through voluntary devotion. Discover how two dedicated complementary bodies safeguard the monument’s physical fabric and welcome the community.

Structure Explained

Understanding Our Dual Entity Governance

To ensure legal integrity and long-term conservation, the management of Grace Dieu Priory is divided into two distinct, cooperative bodies.

Property Holding BodyFormed 1995

The Grace Dieu Priory Trust

Site Owners & Conservation Custodians

Formed in 1995 to rescue the collapsing, ivy-strangled masonry, the Trust is a registered charitable trust company that holds the legal freehold property title to the priory monument and Rusty Mary’s field.

Core Responsibilities:
  • Holds the permanent freehold ownership of the site (purchased in Nov 2024).
  • Oversees major capital conservation, structural masonry stabilization, and statutory consents.
  • Manages future capital developments, including the planned pedestrian footbridge.
  • Enforces site protection bylaws, including the strict ban on paranormal investigations.
Governed by volunteer trustees including local historians and chartered professionals.
Operational CharityFormed 2006

The Friends of Grace Dieu Priory

Registered Charity No. 1117921

Established when the restored ruins officially opened to the public in 2006, the Friends are the active community association responsible for running day-to-day operations and community engagement.

Core Responsibilities:
  • Keeps the ruins open to the public free of charge 365 days a year from dawn to dusk.
  • Organizes volunteer working parties for grounds maintenance, litter clearance, and path care.
  • Delivers public events, including the Medieval Fayre, Carols in the Cloisters, and guided walks.
  • Provides tailored school visits and educational tours with local historians.
Funded 100% by member subscriptions, publication sales, and community donations. No statutory funding.
International Heritage Alliance

Official Partners of Charnwood Forest Geopark

The Friends of Grace Dieu Priory are proud official partners of the Charnwood Forest Geopark, an ambitious regional initiative celebrating the ancient Precambrian geology, unique wildlife, and rich cultural heritage of Leicestershire as it strives toward prestigious UNESCO Global Geopark designation.

The Geopark team and their volunteer working parties have provided vital hands-on support to Grace Dieu over recent years—assisting with path clearances, maintaining woodland biodiversity, and helping expose our intact 800-year-old medieval priory boundary wall during joint working sessions.

Explore the Charnwood Geopartner NetworkWorking towards UNESCO Global Geopark status

Official Partnership Presentation

FOGDP trustees formally receiving official Geopark partner recognition.

Anniversary Milestone · 2006–2026

Celebrating 20 Years of Open Public Access

When the conserved priory was formally opened to the public in 2006, few imagined how vibrant this volunteer sanctuary would become. Over two decades, our small group has hosted tens of thousands of school children, families, living history reenactors, and local walkers.

Every penny raised from our book sales and membership dues goes directly into the stonework and grounds. No paid staff, no corporate bureaucracy—just neighbors keeping history alive.

Visitor Code

Leave No TracePlease take all of your litter home with you. There are no public waste bins on the ancient monument ruins.
Dog WalkersDogs welcome on leads. A dedicated bin is located at the Bull's Head car park for dog litter bags (strictly none on-site).
Strict Site Policy: Paranormal events and ghost walks are expressly forbidden by the Grace Dieu Priory Trust across the entire priory site and surrounding lands.
